drug_class: Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitor (NRTI) — antiretroviral medication
purpose: Abacavir is used to treat HIV, the virus that causes AIDS. It helps lower the amount of HIV in your body so your immune system can stay stronger. It does not cure HIV, but it helps you stay healthier and reduces the risk of passing the virus to others.
how_it_works: HIV needs to copy itself inside your body to keep spreading. Abacavir blocks a tool the virus uses called reverse transcriptase, which the virus needs to make copies of itself. By blocking this step, the medication slows down how fast the virus multiplies in your body.
common_side_effects: Nausea, headache, tiredness, and generally feeling unwell, especially in the first few weeks. Some people may also experience diarrhea, loss of appetite, or trouble sleeping.
warnings: IMPORTANT: A small number of people — especially those with a gene called HLA-B*5701 — can have a serious, potentially life-threatening allergic reaction to abacavir. Your doctor should test you for this gene before you start. Signs of a reaction include fever, rash, nausea, vomiting, or trouble breathing. If this happens, stop the medication and call your doctor immediately — do NOT restart it. Also tell your doctor if you have heart disease, as abacavir may slightly increase heart attack risk.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 600 mg once a day OR 300 mg twice a day, taken with or without food. Your doctor will decide which schedule is best for you. Always take it exactly as prescribed and never skip doses, as this can make the medication stop working.
